page.seoDescription: Two free self-check tools: an insurance-cover check in a few short questions, and a calculator showing how much your management fees cost over your years of saving. No sign-up and no obligation.
page.title: Self-check tools
page.intro: Two tools you can run on your own, without leaving your details and without obligation. They give a general picture and are no substitute for a personal check — that is what the meeting is for.
lead.title: Would you like Dorit to check your real figures?
lead.text: The result here is a general estimate only, not advice or a recommendation. The message opens in WhatsApp with the result, and you can edit it before sending.
lead.send: Send Dorit the result on WhatsApp
assess.title: Which insurance really suits you?
assess.intro: Four short questions — and you'll get a clear picture of the kinds of insurance relevant to your stage of life. This isn't financial advice, just a first map for understanding your needs.
assess.general: This estimate is general only. For precise recommendations, talk to Dorit.
assess.disclaimer: This tool is for a first estimate only and is not financial advice or a recommendation to buy a product. Precise recommendations are given only in a personal meeting.
assess.count: {n} kinds of insurance relevant to you
assess.priorities: {n} of them are recommended as high priority, based on your answers.
assess.noPriority: Based on your answers, these are the kinds of insurance worth looking at.
fee.intro: Management fees look small each month, but over the years they roll up into hundreds of thousands of shekels out of your savings. This calculator gives an honest picture — because knowing is the first step towards an informed decision.
fee.estimate: A general estimate only — no substitute for personal advice.
fee.ask: Want to know whether you could save? Ask me
fee.sumWithout: . With no management fees at all, the balance would be
fee.sumKept: that stays with the managing body instead of with you.
assess.q.stage.label: What stage of life are you at?
assess.q.stage.hint: Your current stage shapes the priorities
assess.q.work.label: How do you work?
assess.q.work.hint: How you're employed changes the protection you need
assess.q.mortgage.label: Do you have a mortgage or significant loans?
assess.q.mortgage.hint: Large commitments call for protecting the family
assess.q.health.label: Any chronic illness or family risk?
assess.q.health.hint: Medical background affects the recommended scope of cover
assess.why.life.parent: Children depend on your income — life insurance makes sure they're protected even if something happens.
assess.why.life.mortgage: A large mortgage remains even without you — life insurance protects the family from the financial burden.
assess.why.life.couple: Your partner depends on your shared income — basic protection is worth securing.
assess.why.health.history: A family medical history makes cover for private medicine, medicines and treatments outside the basic basket more important.
assess.why.health.general: Even good health needs private medicine, treatments and medicines outside the basic basket.
assess.why.disability.selfEmployed: If a self-employed person can't work because of illness or an accident, the income stops entirely. This is the most critical insurance for you.
assess.why.disability.family: When the family depends on your income and there's a mortgage, loss-of-working-capacity cover protects your ability to keep meeting your commitments.
assess.why.accidents: Cover for bodily injury from accidents — especially relevant for the self-employed, who aren't protected through an employer.
assess.why.pension.retiree: Ahead of retirement it's important to review your savings products, management fees and retirement tracks — to make the most of your pension income.
assess.why.pension.parent: With children at home, saving for retirement is easy to put off — yet the management fees and the track chosen in these years add up to tens of thousands of shekels by retirement.
assess.why.critical: A family history justifies critical-illness cover — a one-off payment that helps you cope financially during a health crisis.
assess.why.review: Many employees pay high management fees without knowing it — it's worth reviewing your existing products and lowering costs.
